subject.title: WebChat: a config-change gateway restart drops the in-flight turn (empty/failed session, recovery can't resume, no user notice)

question: Should the linked non-deliverable WebChat notice fix be accepted as the closure path for this issue, or should closure require a broader turn-preservation fix such as restart deferral or immediate inbound-message persistence?
rationale: The source-level bug is real, but the issue asks for any of several remedies and current labels already mark product-direction uncertainty; automation should not choose the final restart-recovery UX contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept notice fix now
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95154 as the scoped fix for blank WebChat recovery, while tracking stronger turn preservation separately if desired.

options.title: Broaden before closure
options.body: Require the fix vehicle to also prove restart deferral or immediate user-message persistence so the in-flight user request is not lost before closing this issue.

options.title: Supersede into recovery redesign
options.body: Keep this issue open but make a broader restart-recovery item the canonical implementation path if maintainers want a no-retype or recover-and-confirm policy instead of the narrow notice mitigation.

recommendation.title: Accept notice fix now
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95154 as the scoped fix for blank WebChat recovery, while tracking stronger turn preservation separately if desired.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the central recovery failure-notice behavior and are the clearest history owner for deciding whether the no-notice branch is enough to close this report.
